static_traits.name: Lin Wei
static_traits.social_status: Lacking Social support; Relationship tension with people who know about the troubles
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; have not received similar psychotherapy before; no prior spelling- or self-blame-related problems
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to describe situations and feelings specifically; negative-leaning thinking, repeated self-blame; skeptical about change but willing to try; speech rate Not mentioned

basic_info.main_problem: I have always felt guilt and self-blame about my current spelling ability.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because I realized self-blame and guilt are affecting my daily life and causing significant suffering.
growth_experiences: Won a spelling bee in Third grade, since then treating past success as a standard to maintain forever; when spelling is not as good as before, blaming self entirely, and sinking into Guilt and self-blame long-term.
Marital history of Multiple divorces, with Interpersonal tension and Weak social support; these experiences worsened the damage to self-esteem and confidence.

special_situations.event: Needs to send emails or fill out reports at work
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If any spelling error appears, it means I am not competent, I failed
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Forcibly ignores negative emotions, toughing it out to complete the task
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: It is my fault; I should keep practicing all along, otherwise I mess it up

special_situations.event: Needing to write a work memo
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot spell perfectly like in Third grade, it means I have regressed and am unforgivable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Temporarily easing Anxiety by being distracted by other Work or tasks
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Every error is being magnified; I am not as good as my past self

special_situations.event: Encountering any task requiring spelling (writing emails, filling forms, writing reports, etc.)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot spell well now, it proves I am just incompetent, and will always be so
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying to ignore and push through
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I always mess up; the future will be like this too

special_situations.event: Recalling winning a spelling bee in third grade
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Past success set the standard I must always reach; falling below this standard equals failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Belittling or denying any current positive changes, focusing on errors
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: That win does not count; current mistakes prove I am a failure

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized as capable, to maintain past excellent performance to safeguard self-esteem
core_conflict.fear: Fears failure and criticism, leading to collapse of self-worth and disappointing others
defense_goal: Maintains a sense of control over mistakes through self-blame
Repressing emotions and pushing through tasks to avoid exposing vulnerability

object_relations.object_representation: A harsh judge who magnifies mistakes

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes trying behavioral experiments or changing cognitions
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing that no matter what I do, it is useless; I will end up back at square one (change is ineffective)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using a steady, Empathetic tone, acknowledging their doubt, inviting a 'small-step attempts' framework, emphasizing not judging by success or failure, only gathering experience.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked about specific mistakes or when self-blame and guilt are discussed
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Blames all mistakes on herself to avoid facing possible evaluation or criticism from others
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Avoiding Reinforcement of self-blame, using gentle reflection and restatement, Guiding distinction between facts and evaluations, and encouraging self-compassion statements.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about the gap between past success and the present
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Taking past external standards as absolute rules without digestion (must always be perfect)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Inquiring in a curious and respectful tone about the source and applicable scope of that standard, inviting a re-evaluation using a continuum and concrete evidence.

manifestations: Lacking a strong Social support system to discuss Self-blame and guilt
Relationship tension with people who know about the troubles
outcomes: Anxiety and Sense of frustration worsening
Falling into a negative thought cycle

manifestations: Feeling that no matter what I do, I will end up back at square one

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Frequently using self-Demands like 'I should keep practicing all the time'
Takes past success as an absolute standard that must always be maintained

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'. Language manifestations include: 'It is all my fault that he was hurt', 'I do not deserve to talk to him', and so on
manifestations: Repeatedly blaming self and thinking 'It is all my fault'
Cautious and skeptical about trying change, worries about failing again

positive_force: Won a spelling bee in third grade, showing basic language and spelling ability
Able to clearly describe the problem cycle (the pattern of identifying self-blame - Anxiety - further self-blame)
Willing to try small behavioral experiments to test beliefs
negative_force: Cognitive biases are marked (Should Statements, Mental Filtering, Overgeneralization, Disqualifying the Positive, etc.)
Judging current performance by past perfect standards, causing Impaired self-esteem

target_behavior.behavior: Marked Anxiety and self-blame when spelling is needed
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalizing Third grade's success as a perfect standard to maintain forever, catastrophizing current errors with all-or-nothing judgments and complete self-attribution
target_behavior.function: Escapes external evaluation and shame (gaining a sense of control by enduring through self-blame and ignoring emotions)
target_behavior.consequence: Declining self-esteem and confidence, Focus and efficiency impaired in Work and Learning, Interpersonal tension

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids emotions and forcibly ignores them, grits through tasks
antecedent: Feeling guilty and Anxious when facing spelling tasks
target_behavior.core_reason: Worrying that directly facing negative emotions will worsen suffering, believing only Repressing emotions allows continuing Work
target_behavior.function: Avoiding stopping to face Anxiety, maintaining superficial task completion
target_behavior.consequence: Intensifying negative emotions, forming a repeated vicious cycle of self-blame - Anxiety - pushing through
